conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be taking care of you tonight. Can you tell me what brought you to the hospital?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi, Doctor. I woke up this morning feeling off. My stomach hurt, and then I started getting nauseous. I vomited a few hours later, and it just kept getting worse.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. How often were you vomiting? And did anything help, like your usual medications?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Every 15 minutes or so. I took Zofran and Ativan like I usually do, but they didn’t help much this time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. You’ve had this before with your gastroparesis. In the ER, they gave you IV fluids, morphine, and more anti-nausea meds. Your blood pressure was a bit low when you came up, but you’re stable now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it feels better now. The pain and nausea are much less. But I’m so tired of these flares. I was just here five days ago.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand. These episodes are tough. Your labs showed a low bicarbonate level when you arrived—17—which means you had a mild metabolic acidosis. That’s common when you’re dehydrated from vomiting.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that serious? It happened last time too.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s not dangerous in this context. It’s due to dehydration and not eating. We’re giving you IV fluids to correct it. Your repeat lab came back with a normal bicarbonate of 23, so you’re already improving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. So this was just another flare, not something new?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Your exam shows mild tenderness all over the abdomen, but no signs of infection or blockage. Your bowel sounds are present, and you’ve passed gas today, which is good.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been worried it might be my J-tube or something with my stomach not working at all.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The tube is fine. This is still related to your gastroparesis, which we know started after your fundoplication. The gastric emptying scan showed delayed emptying before, and the cause is still unknown.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Right. They’ve slowed my tube feeds recently to try to prevent these flares, but it’s still happening.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll keep you on IV fluids tonight and restart your tube feeds slowly tomorrow. If you tolerate them, we can send you home the same day.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. You made it through the night without nausea or pain. You’ve been tolerating sips and your tube feeds are running at your usual rate without issues.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I feel back to my baseline. Can I go home today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’re going to discharge you. Your labs are stable, and you don’t need any more IV meds. Just keep using your PRN medications as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Great. Do I need to change anything with my meds or feeds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No changes. Continue your levothyroxine, omeprazole, citalopram, and vitamin D as before. Use Zofran or Ativan if nausea returns. And keep your follow-up with Dr. Patel next week.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. And my DNR status is still in place, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ve confirmed your DNR/DNI status, and it’s documented in your chart.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor. I know this is routine for you, but it means a lot to me to be heard.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Of course. We know how frustrating these flares are. You’re doing well managing a tough condition. Call your PCP within a week to check in, and we’re here if things worsen.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks again for taking care of me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. The nurse will bring your discharge papers shortly. Have a safe trip home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will do. I’m just glad I can rest in my own bed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Absolutely. Take care, and we hope to see you only in clinic, not back here.
